blocks.text: Sifat (adjective) kishi yoki narsaning belgisini bildiradi va «qanday?» savoliga javob beradi: **old** (eski, keksa), **nice** (yoqimli), **interesting** (qiziqarli), **cheap** (arzon). Bu mavzu o'zbeklar uchun ancha oson, chunki ikki tilda ham sifat **otdan oldin** turadi: **katta** uy — a **big** house. Lekin uchta farq bor: (1) sifatdan oldin ko'pincha artikl keladi (**a** big house); (2) gapning kesimi sifat bo'lsa, **be** shart (The house **is** big — Uy katta); (3) look, feel, smell kabi fe'llardan keyin ravish emas, sifat ishlatiladi.

rows: look, feel, smell, taste, sound dan keyin
The bridge looks **old**. — Ko'prik eski ko'rinadi.

blocks.text: Sifat ot bilan birga bitta birikma hosil qiladi va doim otdan **oldin** keladi — xuddi o'zbekchadagidek. Artikl yoki boshqa aniqlovchi (a, the, my, this, some) butun birikmaning boshida turadi: **a** cheap ticket, **my** new phone, **this** small village. `a` yoki `an` ni otga emas, undan keyingi so'zga — sifatga qarab tanlaymiz: a car, lekin **an old** car, chunki old unli tovush bilan boshlanadi (65-dars). Sifatni otdan keyin qo'yish («a car old») — xato.

items.text: We stayed in a **small** hotel near the beach.
This is an **interesting** book about the Silk Road.
Tashkent has got **wide** streets and **green** parks.

blocks.text: Inglizcha sifatning shakli hech qachon o'zgarmaydi: birlikda ham, ko'plikda ham, erkak va ayol uchun ham bir xil. Ko'plik qo'shimchasi `-s` faqat otga qo'shiladi: a **red** car → two **red** cars («reds cars» emas). O'zbek tilida ham shunday: **qizil** mashina → **qizil** mashinalar. Rus tilini bilsangiz, «новый — новая — новые» kabi o'zgarishlarni unuting — inglizchada bunday narsa yo'q.
be + sifat: The weather is nice

Sifat otsiz, gapning kesimi bo'lib ham keladi. O'zbekchada «Havo yaxshi», «Ko'cha tor» deganda fe'l kerak emas, inglizchada esa sifatdan oldin **be** (am / is / are, was / were) shart: The weather **is** nice. The street **was** narrow. Bu 1-darsdagi qoidaning davomi: inglizcha gapda fe'lsiz kesim bo'lmaydi. Kesimda ikki sifat bo'lsa, ular orasiga **and** qo'yiladi: The room is **small and dark**.
look, feel, smell, taste, sound + sifat

Bu besh fe'l sezgilar bilan bog'liq: ko'rish (**look**), his qilish yoki ushlash (**feel**), hid (**smell**), ta'm (**taste**), eshitish (**sound**). Ular harakatni emas, **egani** tasvirlaydi — xuddi **be** kabi. Shuning uchun ulardan keyin ravish (`-ly`) emas, **sifat** keladi: You **look tired**, The soup **smells good**. Solishtiring: You **are** tired — «Siz charchagansiz» (aniq bilaman); You **look** tired — «Charchagan ko'rinasiz» (ko'rinishingizdan shunday tuyulyapti).

rows: The lemon tastes **sour**. — Limonning ta'mi nordon.
Your idea sounds **good**. — Fikringiz yaxshi ekan.

blocks.text: Ravish (quickly, slowly, well) egani emas, harakatni — fe'lni tasvirlaydi: He drives **carefully** (ehtiyotkorlik bilan haydaydi). Sifat esa egani: He is **careful**, He looks **careful**. Ravishlar — keyingi, 86-darsda.

Otdan oldin ikki sifat kelsa, odatda avval **fikr** (nice, beautiful, terrible), keyin **fakt** — o'lcham, yosh, rang (big, old, red) aytiladi: a **nice old** house, a **beautiful red** dress, a **big black** dog. Bu holda **and** qo'yilmaydi. be dan keyin esa ikki sifat orasida **and** kerak: The house is **old and beautiful**.

O'zbeklarning tipik xatolari: «a house big» → **a big house**; «beautifuls flowers» → **beautiful flowers** (sifat ko'plikda o'zgarmaydi); «The weather very nice» → **The weather is very nice** (be tushib qolmasin); «You look tiredly», «The soup smells well» → **You look tired**, **The soup smells good**; «I am boring» (Men zerikarli odamman) → **I'm bored** (Zerikdim): `-ing` bilan tugagan sifat narsani tasvirlaydi (a boring film), `-ed` bilan tugagani — odamning holatini.
Eslab qolish: sifat — «qanday?» savoliga javob. U otdan oldin yoki **be / look / feel / smell / taste / sound** dan keyin keladi va hech qachon o'zgarmaydi.

Bog'lanish: something **new**, nothing **special** kabi birikmalar — 79-dars; What's the weather **like**? (Havo qanaqa?) — 46-dars; sifat darajalari: older, more expensive — 87–89-darslar, the oldest — 90-dars.

rows: look / feel / smell / taste / sound + sifat
be dan keyin ikki sifat — and bilan

examples.title: Adjective + noun: **a lovely day**, **an old car**
examples.description: Sifat otdan oldin turadi — o'zbekchadagidek: **katta** uy — a **big** house. Artikl butun birikmadan oldin keladi: **an old** car, **a new** job.

sentences.text: What a **lovely** day!
My uncle still drives an **old** car.
Samarkand is a **beautiful** city with a **long** history.
Do you know a **good** restaurant near here?
Emma has found a **new** job at a **big** bank in London.
It was a **difficult** exam, but I passed it.
sentences.translation: Imtihon **qiyin** edi, lekin men uni topshirdim.

sentences.text: Bekzod lives in a **small** flat on the fifth floor.
We had a **wonderful** holiday in the mountains last summer.
Is there a **cheap** hotel in the centre of Oxford?
Grandma makes **delicious** soup, and everybody loves it.
sentences.translation: Buvim **mazali** sho'rva pishiradi, hamma uni yaxshi ko'radi.

examples.title: Adjectives don't change: **red** apples, **old** friends
examples.description: Inglizcha sifatda ko'plik qo'shimchasi yo'q: a **red** apple — two **red** apples («reds» emas). O'zbekchada ham shunday: **qizil** olma — **qizil** olmalar.

sentences.text: These **red** apples are from our garden.
I've got two **old** friends in Manchester.
Madina bought some **beautiful** flowers for her mother.
Those **black** shoes aren't mine — mine are **brown**.
There are many **tall** buildings in the centre of Tashkent.
Our neighbours are very **kind** people.
In autumn the leaves turn **yellow** and **red**.
Are these eggs **fresh**, or are they from last week?
My brothers are both **clever**, but they're very **lazy**.
The children were **happy** because the lessons were **short** that day.
sentences.translation: O'sha kuni darslar **qisqa** bo'lgani uchun bolalar **xursand** edi.

examples.title: **be** + adjective: The weather **is warm**
examples.description: Sifat **be** (am / is / are, was / were) dan keyin ham keladi: The room **is small**. O'zbekchada fe'lsiz: «Xona kichik», inglizchada **be** shart.

sentences.text: The weather **is warm** and **sunny** today.
Is the museum **free** on Sundays? — Yes, it is.
This chair **isn't comfortable** at all.
Were the questions **easy**? — No, they were really **hard**.
Sarah's flat **is small**, but it's very **clean**.
Why are you so **quiet** today, Aziz?
Last winter was very **cold** in Tashkent.
The streets in the old town **are narrow** and **busy**.
Everybody is **tired**, so let's stop for a cup of tea.
sentences.translation: Hamma **charchagan**, keling, bir piyola choy uchun to'xtaylik.

sentences.text: The test **wasn't difficult**, but it was very **long**.
sentences.translation: Test **qiyin emas** edi, lekin juda **uzun** edi.

examples.title: **look** + adjective: You **look tired**
examples.description: **look** + sifat — «... ko'rinadi»: tashqi ko'rinishga qarab baho beramiz. Bu yerda ravish (tiredly) emas, sifat keladi: You **look tired**.

sentences.text: You **look tired**. Are you OK?
Your new jacket **looks great**!
Does this dress **look nice** on me? — Yes, it does.
James **looked worried** when he came out of the office.
The sky **looks dark** — it's going to rain.
Madina's grandmother **looks young** for her age.
Why do you **look** so **sad**? — I've lost my keys.
sentences.translation: Nega bunchalik **xafa ko'rinasan**? — Kalitlarimni yo'qotib qo'ydim.

sentences.text: From the plane, the city **looked** very **small**.
Those mountains **look close**, but they're fifty kilometres away.
sentences.translation: Anavi tog'lar **yaqin ko'rinadi**, lekin ular ellik kilometr narida.

sentences.text: The food **looked strange**, but it was actually very tasty.
sentences.translation: Taom **g'alati ko'rinardi**, aslida esa juda mazali edi.

examples.title: **feel** + adjective: I **feel sick**
examples.description: **feel** + sifat — o'z holatingiz (I **feel tired**) yoki narsa ushlaganda qanday ekani (The towel **feels soft**). O'zbekchada ko'pincha fe'l bilan: «charchadim», «sovqotyapman».

sentences.text: I **feel sick** — I think it was the fish.
How do you **feel** today? — I **feel fine**, thanks.
After the long walk we all **felt hungry**.
This towel **feels** very **soft**.
Dilnoza **felt nervous** before her first interview.
Don't you **feel cold** in that thin jacket?
On holiday I always **feel relaxed** and **happy**.
sentences.translation: Ta'tilda o'zimni doim **xotirjam** va **baxtli his qilaman**.

sentences.text: The water **felt warm**, so the children went for a swim.
sentences.translation: Suv **iliq** edi, shuning uchun bolalar cho'milishga tushdi.

sentences.text: When Tom heard the news, he **felt angry** with his friends.
Grandad often **feels lonely** because he lives alone in the village.
sentences.translation: Bobom qishloqda yolg'iz yashagani uchun ko'pincha **o'zini yolg'iz his qiladi**.

examples.title: **smell**, **taste**, **sound** + adjective
examples.description: Hid, ta'm va eshitilgan narsa haqida: **smell good** (hidi yoqimli), **taste sweet** (ta'mi shirin), **sound interesting** (qiziq ekan). Bu fe'llardan keyin ham ravish emas, sifat keladi.

sentences.text: Mmm, the soup **smells good**!
These oranges **taste** very **sweet**.
Your plan **sounds interesting**. Tell me more.
The milk **smells bad** — don't drink it!
Does the coffee **taste bitter** to you?
Aziz's voice **sounded strange** on the phone yesterday.
In spring the whole garden **smells wonderful**.
This medicine **tastes awful**, but it really helps.
sentences.translation: Bu dorining **ta'mi juda yomon**, lekin rosa foyda qiladi.

sentences.text: A weekend in Bukhara? That **sounds lovely**!
sentences.translation: Dam olish kunlari Buxoroda? Bu **juda zo'r-ku**!

sentences.text: The bread **smelled fresh**, but it **tasted** a bit **dry**.
sentences.translation: Nondan **yangi hid** kelardi, lekin **ta'mi** biroz **quruq** edi.

examples.title: Opposites: **isn't cheap**, it's **expensive**
examples.description: Qarama-qarshi sifatlar juft-juft eslab qolinadi. Inkor va uning qarama-qarshisi yonma-yon: It **isn't cheap** — it's **expensive**.

sentences.text: The shop on the corner **isn't cheap** — it's quite **expensive**.
Is your new boss **strict**? — No, she's very **easy-going**.
Our first flat was **dark** and **noisy**, but this one is **light** and **quiet**.
sentences.translation: Birinchi kvartiramiz **qorong'i** va **shovqinli** edi, bunisi esa **yorug'** va **tinch**.

sentences.text: The river **isn't deep** here, so we can walk across it.
sentences.translation: Bu yerda daryo **chuqur emas**, shuning uchun kechib o'tsak bo'ladi.

sentences.text: Bekzod's suitcase was **heavy**, but mine was **light**.
That road was **dangerous** in winter, but now it's **safe**.
sentences.translation: Ilgari u yo'l qishda **xavfli** edi, endi esa **xavfsiz**.

sentences.text: Is the pool **open** today? — No, it's **closed** for repairs.
Our teacher **isn't old** — she's only twenty-six.
sentences.translation: O'qituvchimiz **keksa emas** — atigi yigirma olti yoshda.

sentences.text: The film **wasn't boring** at all — it was really **exciting**.
sentences.translation: Film umuman **zerikarli emas** edi — juda **qiziqarli** edi.

sentences.text: In Samarkand the days are **hot**, but the nights are surprisingly **cool**.

examples.title: Dialogue: **a lovely new flat**
examples.description: Aralash mustahkamlash: sifat + ot (a **quiet** street), **be** + sifat (it's **bright**), **look** / **sound** + sifat va something **delicious**.

sentences.text: — So, how's your **new** flat, Dilnoza?
— It's **lovely**! It's **small**, but it's very **bright**.
— Is it **quiet**? Your old flat was so **noisy**.
— Yes, it's on a **quiet** street near a **big** park.
— That **sounds perfect**. And what are the neighbours like?
— They seem **friendly**. The woman next door is a **retired** teacher.
— And the kitchen? You love cooking **big** dinners.
sentences.translation: — Oshxona-chi? Sen **katta** dasturxon yozishni yaxshi ko'rasan-ku.

sentences.text: — The kitchen is **modern**, and the cooker is **brand new**.
— You **look** really **happy** about it!
— I am! Come on Saturday — I'll make something **delicious**.
sentences.translation: — Ha, xursandman! Shanba kuni kel — **mazali** bir narsa pishiraman.
